description: The plot, titled "Hidden State Mean," illustrates the evolution of the absolute mean of hidden states across different layers in a neural network, comparing three distinct metrics: the mean before the gate, the mean after the gate, and the baseline mean. The x-axis, labeled "Layer," spans from 0 to 25, representing the sequential layers of the model, while the y-axis, labeled "Abs Mean," measures the absolute mean of the hidden states, ranging from 0 to 4. The blue dashed line, representing the "hidden state mean before gate," starts at a value of approximately 0.1 and remains relatively stable until layer 20, after which it experiences a sharp increase, reaching a peak of approximately 4.3 at layer 25. The orange dotted line, representing the "hidden state mean after gate," begins at a value of approximately 0.05 and remains nearly flat, showing a slight increase to about 0.1 at layer 25. The green solid line, representing the "hidden state mean of baseline," starts at a value of approximately 0.02 and remains nearly flat, showing a slight increase to about 0.1 at layer 25. The legend indicates that the average values for the "hidden state mean before gate," "hidden state mean after gate," and "hidden state mean of baseline" are 0.71, 0.05, and 0.04, respectively. The plot shows that the mean of the hidden states before the gate increases significantly in the later layers, while the mean after the gate and the baseline remain relatively stable.
